question.text: SEBI (Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations, commonly known as PFUTP, prohibit:

answer.text: Market manipulation, price rigging, circular trading, and spreading misleading information to induce trading
Legitimate trading activities during volatile markets

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI (Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations - PFUTP - broadly prohibit any device, scheme or artifice that defrauds or manipulates the securities market. The standard prohibited categories include manipulating the price of securities, creating artificial trading volume through circular or wash trades, spreading false or misleading information to induce trading, front-running large client orders, and any other practice deemed fraudulent or unfair. PFUTP applies across the cash and derivatives segments. The Trap: Insider trading is governed primarily by a separate framework (the SEBI PIT Regulations), so "only insider trading" is too narrow. Legitimate trading during volatile markets is not, by itself, manipulation. Short selling by retail investors under exchange rules is a permitted activity, not a PFUTP violation. Note: The specific PFUTP prohibition list (circular trading, wash trades, misleading information) is not laid out in the cited pages of the NISM-Series-VIII Equity Derivatives workbook, which on the pages checked supports SEBI's broad power to prohibit fraudulent and unfair practices and lists stockbroker suspension grounds (manipulation, price rigging, cornering the market). The framing above is general SEBI PFUTP regulatory knowledge.
